articles.summary: Nvidia’s board is investigating Jensen Huang over his relationship with a suspected Chinese spy, and Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld thinks it’s roughly a coin flip whether Huang stays on as CEO.
articles.title: Is Jensen Huang’s job on the line? Yale’s Jeffrey Sonnenfeld estimates it’s “about a 50-50”

articles.summary: In an interview filmed on October 14, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang defended engaging with China and criticized US chip restrictions. He has since acknowledged having an affair, and US intelligence officials reportedly suspect the woman was recruited by Beijing to influence him. Nvidia’s board is now investigating, and Huang said he would "cooperate fully." He spoke with Bloomberg’s Emily Chang for an upcoming episode of The Circuit. (Source: Bloomberg)
articles.title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang: China Is 'Not Our Enemy,' US Chip Policy a 'Mistake'

articles.summary: Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang has admitted he had an affair. The woman was identified in a series of reports as a suspected Chinese spy, plunging the chip colossus into a crisis like none before in its three-decade history. (Source: Bloomberg)

Bloomberg's Minmin Low breaks down the news and shares what Huang previously told Bloomberg about the company's succession plans. (Source: Bloomberg)
